C08-M02-L01-F1.title: Endpoint telemetry: sources, control points and collection
C08-M02-L01-F1.caption: Where endpoint events are produced on a host, which settings filter them, and how they reach the SIEM.
C08-M02-L01-F1.alt: Graph diagram. Activity on the host (processes, files, registry, logons) feeds four sources: the Security log (4624, 4625, 4688, 4720, 4732, 1102), PowerShell Operational (4103 module, 4104 script block), Sysmon/Operational (events 1, 3, 11, 12-14, 22 with ProcessGuid) and the EDR agent (telemetry plus own detections). Audit policy filters the Security log; the Sysmon XML config filters Sysmon. The EDR agent has a dashed response arrow back to the host activity. A Linux host (auth.log, journal, auditd) is a further source. All sources send events to the Collector / forwarder (agent, WEF or syslog), which sends parsed, normalised events to the SIEM (search, correlate, retain).

nodes.label: Audit policy
nodes.sub: decides what the Security log records

C08-M02-L01-F1.note: An event reaches the SOC only if a source observed it, its configuration allowed it and the forwarder shipped it.
